counterfactual_missing_items: explicit multifocal or recurrent bone involvement is not stated; only the left femoral lesion is described
no direct biopsy of the sclerotic femoral lesion itself was reported; the histology was from an open synovial biopsy
no CRMO-specific extraskeletal clues such as palmoplantar pustulosis, clavicular involvement, or documented NSAID response are given
decisive_items: mild to moderate chronic synovitis with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates
a well-defined T1-hypointense, STIR-hyperintense lesion with a thick sclerotic rim in the anterolateral cortex of the left femoral head
He received 6 months of empirical anti-tubercular therapy without clinical improvement
response.rationale: R3 best explains the whole raw picture: a chronic locally destructive bone lesion with sterile lymphoplasmacytic inflammation, negative cultures, and failure of anti-tubercular therapy. R1 explains the pain and femoral lesion but lacks direct histologic evidence of Langerhans-cell infiltrates. R2 has no sarcoma-specific malignant tissue or soft-tissue mass, and R5 accounts only for nonspecific synovial reaction. R3 remains imperfect because the multifocal/recurrent label is not explicit, hence medium margin.

rejected.why: The raw supports only reactive synovitis; there are no intra-articular cartilaginous or bony loose bodies and the femoral cortical lesion is unexplained.
The histology is bland chronic lymphoplasmacytic inflammation, not a biphasic malignant sarcoma; no soft-tissue mass or sarcoma-specific raw finding is present.
